newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks stage comeback after Greenspan jolt.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks stage comeback after Greenspan jolt.

text.p: Tokyo stocks staged a comeback by the end of the Thursday session, recovering from the morning's losses which came in reaction to warnings by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan over dramatic advances on Wall Street, brokers said.
The 225-share Nikkei average edged back above the 19,000 level to finish 30.64 points, or 0.16 percent higher at 19,021.56. Its March futures, however, lost 40 points to 18,990.
Trade was fairly thin, but blue-chip issues were well sought after, helping to brighten market sentiment, they said.
Turnover was a modest 308 million shares, compared with 383 million on Wednesday. Losers outpaced winners 685 to 394, while 167 issues were unchanged.

"The budget for the next fiscal year is due to be passed next week and until that's over, there won't be any cues from the political arena the market can move on," said Masayuki Matsumoto, an analyst at Dai-ichi Securities.
Brokers said once sure way to boost the Nikkei average further and keep it above the 19,000 level would be government measures to improve the liquidity of the stagnant property market.
Shares in the bank sector 0#BNK.T, which were bought back in recent sessions, eased as the buying may have peaked out.
Sakura Bank lost 22 yen to 788 yen.

Construction firm Tobishima Corp rose on reports that Yasuda Trust and Banking Co Ltd had decided to write off bad loans including those extended to the Tobishima group. It added five to end at 181 yen.
Sea transport O#SHP.T shares sank 1.50 percent, hit by news the U.S. Maritime Commission would impose $100,000 port surcharges on Japanese vessels calling at U.S. ports.
Mitsui OSK Lines fell six yen to 249.
